title: Our Eyes Are on You
subtitle: 1 & 2 Chronicles in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
The books of Chronicles begin with a long list of names and end with a door swung open. In between: a man named for sorrow who asked not to pass it on, gatekeepers opening the house morning by morning, singers who never stopped, the ark coming home with cymbals and harps, a loaf and a raisin cake for everyone, an old king saying all things come from you, trumpets and voices becoming one sound, a nation told to humble itself and pray, singers walking ahead of an army, a chest by the gate filling with gifts, a proud king humbled in chains and brought home, and a land left quiet to keep its Sabbaths.

This book walks through it in thirty-six short poems, in five parts: the names, the ark and the song, David's charge and offering, Solomon to Jehoshaphat, and the last kings to Cyrus's decree. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the story touches—a potter's jar, a bronze cymbal, a cake of raisins, an empty pair of fetters—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the books of Chronicles alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: Adam, Seth, Enosh
paintings.epigraph: “Adam, Seth, Enosh”
paintings.poem:
the book opens
with a list.

no garden, no flood.
just names,
one after another,
like stones laid down
to cross a river.

Adam. Seth. Enosh.

whoever wrote them down
was writing after the exile,
counting what was left.

and the first thing counted
was people.

before the temple,
before the kings,
a name.

paintings.title: the potters
paintings.epigraph: “These were the potters”
paintings.poem:
tucked among the fathers and sons
of Judah,
a small note:

a house of linen workers.
the potters.
they lived there with the king
for his work.

no battles.
no prophecies.
just flax and clay,
and hands that knew
how to turn a wheel.

somebody thought
they were worth
writing down.

they were.

paintings.title: Jabez
paintings.epigraph: “God granted him that which he requested.”
paintings.poem:
his mother named him
for her pain.

he carried that name
every day,
in every call to supper,
in every greeting at the gate.

then one day
he called on God himself.

bless me indeed.
enlarge my border.
let your hand be with me.
keep me from evil,
that I may not cause pain.

a boy named for sorrow,
asking not to pass it on.

God granted him
that which he requested.

paintings.title: keepers of the thresholds
paintings.epigraph: “to their duty was its opening morning by morning.”
paintings.poem:
two hundred twelve of them,
listed by name in their villages,
and all of them
keepers of the door.

east, west, north, south.

they counted the vessels in.
they counted the vessels out.
they stayed around God's house
through the night,

and every morning
they opened it.

a whole life
spent making sure
the door would open.

paintings.title: day and night
paintings.epigraph: “they were employed in their work day and night.”
paintings.poem:
some of them baked the bread,
every Sabbath.

some of them mixed the spices.

and some of them sang,
and did nothing else,
because the singing
never stopped.

day and night.

somewhere in the house,
while the city slept,
a voice was still going,
still giving thanks.

you did not have to be awake
for it to be true.

paintings.title: three months
paintings.epigraph: “Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom’s house and all that he had.”
paintings.poem:
the oxen stumbled.
a man put out his hand.
and the joy of that day
ended at a threshing floor.

David was afraid.
how can I bring God's ark
home to me?

so it went aside
to another man's house.
Obed-Edom the Gittite.

three months.

and something in that house
got quietly, steadily
better.

the thing the king was afraid of
was a blessing
in a smaller house.

paintings.title: he taught the singers
paintings.epigraph: “He taught the singers, because he was skillful.”
paintings.poem:
before the ark could move again,
somebody had to rehearse.

the names are all there.
Heman, Asaph, Ethan.
cymbals of bronze.
harps tuned
to the eight-stringed lyre.

and over the singing,
Chenaniah.
he taught the singers,
because he was skillful.

this time the ark came home
carried by the Levites,
lifted by voices
that had practiced.

worship is a gift.
it is also
somebody's careful work.22

paintings.title: a loaf and a raisin cake
paintings.epigraph: “to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.”
paintings.poem:
the ark was set in the tent.
the offerings were made.
the king blessed the people
in Yahweh's name.

and then he fed them.

everyone.
man and woman.
a loaf,
a portion,
a cake of raisins.

nobody went home
from that day
with empty hands.

that is how you know
it was a holy day.

the bread
came with it.

paintings.title: seek his face
paintings.epigraph: “Seek Y ahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more.”
paintings.poem:
on that day
David first ordained
to give thanks
by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.

the song began with a call.
give thanks.
call on his name.
tell what he has done.

then it kept going.
seek him.
seek his strength.
seek his face.

forever more.

it was written
for a single day.

it was meant
for every day after.

paintings.title: the trees of the forest
paintings.epigraph: “Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before Yahweh”
paintings.poem:
let the sea roar.
let the field exult.

the song doesn't stay
with the singers in linen
and the harps.

it goes out past the tent,
past the city,
into the hills,

where the oaks
are already moving
in the wind.

he is good.
his loving kindness
endures forever.

the trees
were singing it
before we were.

paintings.title: prepared abundantly
paintings.epigraph: “So David prepared abundantly before his death.”
paintings.poem:
he would never see it.
he knew that.

the house was for his son.
young and tender, he said,
and the house must be
exceedingly magnificent.

so he did the part he could.
stone.
timber.
bronze and iron without weight,
stacked and waiting.

some of us are given
the finishing.

some of us are given
the gathering,
for a house
someone else will walk into.

both are the work.

paintings.title: the small as well as the great
paintings.epigraph: “the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student.”
paintings.poem:
two hundred eighty-eight singers,
all of them skillful.

and when it came time
to choose who would serve when,
they cast lots,

all alike.

no one sang first
because of a name.
no one waited
because of an age.

the old master
and the one still learning
took their turn
from the same hand.

paintings.title: he will be found
paintings.epigraph: “If you seek him, he will be found by you”
paintings.poem:
the father's charge
was not about the building.

know the God of your father.
serve him with a perfect heart,
a willing mind.

he searches all hearts.
he understands
every thought
you haven't said yet.

and then a promise,
tucked inside the warning:

if you seek him,
he will be found by you.

not hidden.
not far.

a door
that was never locked.

paintings.title: offered willingly
paintings.epigraph: “with a perfect heart they offered willingly to Y ahweh”
paintings.poem:
who offers willingly?
the king asked.

and they came.
leaders of houses.
captains of thousands.
people with precious stones
they had been keeping.

gold, silver, bronze, iron.

but what the story remembers
is not the weight of it.

the people rejoiced,
because they gave
with a whole heart.

a gift like that
makes the giver glad
before it builds
anything at all.

paintings.title: of your own
paintings.epigraph: “For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.”
paintings.poem:
the gifts were piled high,
more than anyone there
had ever seen.

and David looked at it all
and said,
who am I,
and what is my people?

all things come from you.
we have given you
of your own.

like a child
bringing a father
fruit from the father's tree.

the gift is still a gift.

it was just
never ours
to begin with.

paintings.title: as a shadow
paintings.epigraph: “Our days on the earth are as a shadow”
paintings.poem:
in the middle of the celebration,
with the gold piled high,
the old king said:

we are strangers before you,
and foreigners,
as all our fathers were.
our days are a shadow.

not bitter.
just true.

and then he prayed,
not for the gold to last,
but for the wanting to.

keep this desire forever
in the hearts of your people.

he knew
what outlasts a shadow.

paintings.title: just to burn incense
paintings.epigraph: “Who am I then, that I should build him a house, except just to burn incense before him?”
paintings.poem:
the letter to Tyre
asked for cedar and cypress
and people who knew gold.

and in the middle of the order,
a confession.

heaven can't contain him.
the heaven of heavens can't.
who am I to build him a house?

except
just to burn incense before him.

that was the whole temple.
all that cedar,
all that gold,
a place to stand
and send up something small
and fragrant
to someone too big
for the room.46

paintings.title: one sound
paintings.epigraph: “when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard”
paintings.poem:
a hundred twenty trumpets.
cymbals, harps, strings.
singers in fine linen.

a lot of sound
from a lot of people.

and then the moment
it all became
one sound.

for he is good.
his loving kindness endures forever.

that was when the cloud came.

not when the gold was hung.
not when the doors were set.

when all those voices
finally agreed.

paintings.title: when you hear, forgive
paintings.epigraph: “Y es, hear from your dwelling place, even from heaven; and when you hear, forgive.”
paintings.poem:
the king knelt
and spread his hands toward heaven,

and his prayer
was mostly about
other people's prayers.

the foreigner from a far country.
the soldier sent out on the road.
the captive in a strange land,
turning toward home.

when they pray toward this place,
hear.
and when you hear,
forgive.

he built the house
so that anyone, anywhere,
could face it
and be heard.

paintings.title: if my people
paintings.epigraph: “if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves”
paintings.poem:
the answer came at night,
after the crowds went home.

if the sky shuts,
if the locusts come,

the way back starts
with my people,
the ones called by my name.

humble yourselves.
pray.
seek my face.
turn.

four small doors.

and behind them,
three things only God can do.

hear.
forgive.
heal the land.

paintings.title: good things found
paintings.epigraph: “Moreover, there were good things found in Judah.”
paintings.poem:
the gold shields were gone,
carried off to Egypt.
the king made bronze ones
to take their place.

a smaller kingdom.
a humbler king.

and still,
in the middle of the loss,
one line:

there were good things
found in Judah.

when he humbled himself,
the wrath turned.
not everything was lost.

God was still counting
what was good.

paintings.title: no one besides you
paintings.epigraph: “Yahweh, there is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength.”
paintings.poem:
between the mighty
and the one with no strength,
Asa said,
there is no one but you.

it means the gap
is too wide for us.

it also means
the size of the army
matters less
than who stands in the middle.

help us.
we rely on you.
you are our God.
don't let man prevail
against you.

he made the fight
God's.

paintings.title: back and forth
paintings.epigraph: “For Y ahweh’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth”
paintings.poem:
it came as a rebuke.

Asa, who once cried
there is no one but you,
had sent temple silver
to a foreign king
instead of asking.

and still, inside the rebuke,
this:

his eyes run back and forth
through the whole earth,
looking.

not for the strong.
for hearts that are wholly his,
so he can be strong
for them.

you don't have to be big
to be found.

paintings.title: our eyes are on you
paintings.epigraph: “We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
paintings.poem:
the news came.
a great multitude,
already at En Gedi.

the king was alarmed,
and set himself
to seek Yahweh.

he stood in the court
and prayed out loud,
and at the end
he ran out of plans.

we have no might.
we don't know what to do.

but our eyes are on you.

and all Judah stood there,
their little ones beside them,
looking the same way.

paintings.title: the singers went first
paintings.epigraph: “When they began to sing and to praise”
paintings.poem:
they rose early
into the wilderness of Tekoa,
and the king put the singers
in front.

not archers.
not shields.
voices in holy array,
singing the oldest song they had.

give thanks to Yahweh.
his loving kindness endures forever.

when they began to sing,
the battle
was already being fought
by someone else.

they only had
to keep walking
and keep singing.

paintings.title: valley of blessing
paintings.epigraph: “there they blessed Yahweh”
paintings.poem:
they named the valley
for what they did there.

not for the enemy.
not for the fear.

Beracah.
blessing.

then they went home
to Jerusalem
with harps.

paintings.title: the chest by the gate
paintings.epigraph: “All the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had filled it.”
paintings.poem:
the house had been broken up,
its holy things
given away to idols.

the king wanted it mended.
the Levites were slow.

so they set a chest by the gate,
and the people came,
and gave,
and rejoiced,
until it was full.

emptied, and set out again,
day by day.

the house of God
rebuilt
one gift at a time.

paintings.title: much more than this
paintings.epigraph: “Y ahweh is able to give you much more than this.”
paintings.poem:
he had already paid
a hundred talents
to hire an army
God told him not to take.

what about the money?

the man of God
didn't argue the numbers.

he only said,
Yahweh is able
to give you
much more than this.

sometimes obeying
costs what you already spent.

let it go.
it was never
the biggest number
in the room.

paintings.title: the city of palm trees
paintings.epigraph: “gave them sandals, and gave them something to eat and to drink”
paintings.poem:
captives of a war between brothers,
marched north to Samaria.

a prophet stood in the road:
send them back.

and a few men,
their names written down,
did more than that.

they clothed them.
gave them sandals.
food and drink.
oil for their wounds.
the weakest rode donkeys

all the way to Jericho,
the city of palm trees,
to their brothers.

mercy
can be very specific.

paintings.title: he opened the doors
paintings.epigraph: “he opened the doors of Yahweh’s house, and repaired them.”
paintings.poem:
his father had shut them.

Hezekiah didn't wait.
first year.
first month.

he opened the doors
and repaired them.

then the cleaning,
the lamps,
the incense,
and the song begun again
with David's instruments.

the thing was done suddenly.

it can take years
to close a door.

it can take
one morning
to open it.

paintings.title: may the good Y ahweh pardon
paintings.epigraph: “May the good Yahweh pardon everyone”
paintings.poem:
the letters went out:
turn again. come home.

many laughed at the couriers.
some came anyway,
not clean
the way it was written.

they ate the Passover anyway,
and the king prayed:

may the good Yahweh pardon
everyone who sets his heart
to seek God.

and Yahweh listened
and healed the people.

they kept the feast seven days,
and then seven more.

paintings.title: then Manasseh knew
paintings.epigraph: “Then Manasseh knew that Yahweh was God.”
paintings.poem:
he led his people
further wrong
than the nations had gone,
and didn't listen.

then the chains,
the long road to Babylon.

and there,
with nothing left to rule,
he begged.
he humbled himself greatly.

and God
let himself be asked.
heard him.
brought him home.

then Manasseh knew
that Yahweh was God.

it is never too late
to find out.

paintings.title: no longer a burden
paintings.epigraph: “It will no longer be a burden on your shoulders.”
paintings.poem:
at the Passover,
Josiah told the Levites
to set the ark down.

put it in the house.
it will no longer be a burden
on your shoulders.

now serve Yahweh your God,
and his people.

the carrying had been holy.
the rest was holy too.

hands that had held the poles
were free
to hold a lamb,
a cup,
a child's hand
in the crowd.

paintings.title: rising up early
paintings.epigraph: “rising up early and sending, because he had compassion on his people”
paintings.poem:
before the end,
the book stops to say
why it took so long.

God kept sending.
rising up early.
messenger after messenger,

because he had compassion
on his people
and on his dwelling place.

they mocked and scoffed
until there was no remedy,

and the fire came,
and the walls came down.

but read it again.
the longest part of the story
was not the ending.

it was the sending.

paintings.title: the land kept Sabbath
paintings.epigraph: “As long as it lay desolate, it kept Sabbath”
paintings.poem:
the people were gone.
the city was ash.

and the fields,
for the first time in a long time,
rested.

no plow.
no harvest.
seventy years
of Sabbath.

wild grass on the terraces.
flowers no one planted.

even in the ruin,
something God had asked for
was finally
being kept.

paintings.title: let him go up
paintings.epigraph: “Yahweh his God be with him, and let him go up.”
paintings.poem:
the book could have ended
with ash.

it ends
with a door.

a foreign king,
his spirit stirred by God,
put it in writing.

whoever there is among you
of all his people,
Yahweh his God be with him,
and let him go up.

the book that began
with a long list of names
ends
with a space left open

for one more.
